title: The discount round trip
hook: 20% down, then 20% up: will the price return to its starting point?

knows: that a model can declare hypothetical quantities
doesNotKnow: Explain why opposite percentage changes do not cancel.

misconception: Equal percentage increases and decreases cancel out.
objective: Explain why opposite percentage changes do not cancel.

claims.text: B reduces the original price by 20%, then raises that reduced price by 20%. Scaled model; fictional prices; changing percentage base.
claims.source: Declared hypothetical inputs and limits in resource-specs.json. No actual product, price, tariff, shelf-life, treatment or physical appliance specification is asserted. FC LH-1 (session 2, received by message): verified; see company/reviews/lifehacks-200/fact-check-LH1-2026-10-14.md.

claims.text: The stage's two results are computed by the printed expressions. At Original=100€, A=€100 and B=€96. Geometry follows the declared dimension relationships. Other pictures use a fixed full scale across the slider range; continuous fills and arcs show relative amounts rather than literal object counts.
claims.source: src/lib/lifehacks/resource-specs.json contains this lesson's numeric AST; src/lib/lifehacks/resource-model.ts evaluates it. A="x"; B=["*","x",0.8,1.2]; x denotes Original. At x=100, A=100, B=96. Values are fictional/ideal assumptions, not measurements. Display rounds to at most three decimals. Diagram scale: resourceGraphicScale in resource-model.ts takes the maximum modeled magnitude across both formulas and the declared slider range. For non-geometry figures, full-scale values are displayed; the scale stays fixed when the slider changes. Energy axis endpoints use resourceAxisEnd, including B=5×A hours in lh-watts-hours-trade; cylinder rx and ry both scale with radius in resourceCylinderDimensions. FC LH-1 (session 2, received by message): verified; see company/reviews/lifehacks-200/fact-check-LH1-2026-10-14.md.

claims.text: The rise starts from the smaller base. Multiplying 0.8 by 1.2 gives 0.96, so the round trip finishes below the starting price. Equal percentages need not be equal amounts.

claims.text: A fictional €50 price falls by 20%, then rises by 20%. Where does it finish? Correct: €48. The rise starts from €40, so it adds €8, not €10: 0.8 × 1.2 = 0.96 of the start.
